newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Buyers of Brazil Cemig stake see growth potential.
newsitem.headline: Buyers of Brazil Cemig stake see growth potential.

text.p: The U.S.-led group which bought a 32.96 percent voting stake in Minas Gerais state power firm Cemig said the company has the potential to expand its operations to other areas of Brazil.

U.S.-based AES Corp, Southern Electric, unit of Southern Company, and a group of funds formed by Brazilian bank Opportunity bought the Cemig stake for the minimum price of 1.13 billion reais ($1.06 billion).
The stake represents 14.4 percent of the company's total capital.

"We view this association with much expectation for growth," said Luiz David Travesso, AES vice-president in Brazil. "Cemig is in a position to expand its activities and its generating capacity within the state and within the country."

The Cemig sale is being seen as a "de facto" privatization by analysts, who say it will show the company as a gem of Brazil's power sector, and the vice-president of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), Jose Pio Borges, described it as the "third largest privatization" to date.
AES and Southern Electric will have a 90 percent stake in the special purpose company (SPE) which will be formed to administer the Cemig stake, while Opportunity will hold the remaining 10 percent.
Southern Electric Director in Brazil, Claudio Sales, said it was still to be decided how AES and Southern Electric would divide up their joint 90-percent stake.

He said Cemig was Southern Electric's first acquisition in the Brazilian electricity sector and the company was interested in future power sell-offs. AES already owns a stake in Rio de Janeiro power company Light which was privatized last year.
Travesso and Sales said the investor group had no concrete plans for investment, expansion or potential job cuts yet.
"It's premature to speak of future plans," Travesso said. "Investment and expansion plans will be studied jointly and announced in due course. There has been no evaluation as to job cuts."

Minas Gerais state will earn 500 million reais ($467.3 million) from the Cemig sale after paying 580 million reais ($542.1 million) to BNDESpar, the investment arm of the BNDES, to pay off a loan and 50 million reais ($46.7 million) as an auction fee.
Guia said the money would be invested in infrastructure and social projects in Minas Gerais.
The buyers of the Cemig stake will have to pay 50 percent of the sale price by June 3, while the remaining amount can be paid with two promissory notes redeemable within one year after the auction.
